key_insight: A temperature-calibrated in-situ XRD workflow can more reliably identify true phase transitions and decomposition in halide perovskites than uncorrected high-temperature tests.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical validation method for screening thermal stability in inorganic and double perovskite absorber materials used in solar-cell development.
method: Used CsPbCl3 as a baseline reference material for thermal behavior.
Applied in-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction to track phase changes and decomposition.
Used a control substrate and refinements to estimate the true sample temperature during heating.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports phase transitions and decomposition temperatures were directly observed for CsPbCl3 and then used to probe thermal kinetics in Cs2AgSbCl6.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate temperature calibration and reproducible heating conditions, so misestimated sample temperature could distort stability conclusions.
paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
